sanskrit: prāsya dhārā akṣaranvṛṣṇaḥ sutasyaujasā . devāṃ anu prabhūṣataḥ agne tava śravo vayo mahi bhrājante arcayo vibhāvaso . bṛhadbhāno śavasā vājamukthya3ṃ dadhāsi dāśuṣe kave āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaścarṣaṇīnām . saṅkrandano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā ajayatsākamindraḥ
english: The streams of this mighty pressed soma flow with force, adorning the gods. O Agni, your fame and vigor are great; your flames blaze forth, O Vibhavasu. O Far-shining One, by your might you bestow the prize-hymn upon the worshipper, O sage. Swift, whetted, terrible as a bull, striking blow on blow, shaking all peoples — the roaring, unwinking, sole hero Indra conquered a hundred armies at once.

sanskrit: saptiṃ mṛjanti vedhaso gṛṇantaḥ kāravo girā . jyotirjajñānamukthyam pāvakavarcāḥ śukravarcā anūnavarcā udiyarṣi bhānunā . putro mātarā vicarannupāvasi pṛṇakṣi rodasī ubhe saṅkrandanenānimiṣeṇa jiṣṇunā yutkāreṇa duścyavanena dhṛṣṇunā . tadindreṇa jayata tatsahadhvaṃ yudho nara iṣuhastena vṛṣṇā
english: The wise priests, praising with song, rub clean the swift steed. The light that was born, the hymn-prize — with pure radiance, bright splendor, full brilliance you rise with your beam. Like a son moving between two mothers you refresh and fill both worlds. With the roaring, unwinking, victorious, battle-rousing, hard-shaking, bold one — with that Indra conquer; endure in battle, O men, with that arrow-bearing mighty one.

sanskrit: suṣahā soma tāni te punānāya prabhūvaso . vardhā samudramukthyam ūrjo napājjātavedaḥ suśastibhirmandasva dhītibhirhitaḥ . tve iṣaḥ saṃ dadhurbhūrivarpasaścitrotayo vāmajātāḥ sa iṣuhastaiḥ sa niṣaṅgibhirvaśī saṃsraṣṭā sa yudha indro gaṇena . saṃ sṛṣṭajitsomapā bāhuśardhyū3gradhanvā pratihitābhirastā
english: O easy-conquering Soma, easily overcome are those for the purifying one, O lord of abundance; increase the ocean-hymn. O grandson of strength, O Jatavedas, gladden yourself with praises, prompted by thoughts. In you they have stored impulses of many forms, born brightly beautiful. He with arrows in hand, he with quiver, the controller, the mingler — Indra the fighter with his host — the union-winner, soma-drinker, arm-powerful, strong-bowed, shooting in return.

sanskrit: irajyannagne prathayasva jantubhirasme rāyo amartya . sa darśatasya vapuṣo vi rājasi pṛṇakṣi darśataṃ kratum
english: Ruling gloriously, O Agni, spread wide among creatures for us the wealth, O immortal. As such you shine in your visible form of beauty; you fill us with visible wisdom.

sanskrit: iṣkarttāramadhvarasya pracetasaṃ kṣayantaṃ rādhaso mahaḥ . rātiṃ vāmasya subhagāṃ mahīmiṣaṃ dadhāsi sānasiṃ rayim
english: Him who accomplishes the sacrifice, the wise one, the lord of great bounty — you bestow the glorious gift of the beautiful, the great refreshment, the winning wealth.

sanskrit: ṛtāvānaṃ mahiṣaṃ viśvadarśatamagniṃ sumnāya dadhire puro janāḥ . śrutkarṇaṃ saprathastamaṃ tvā girā daivyaṃ mānuṣā yugā
english: The peoples have placed Agni, the upholder of cosmic order, the great bull, visible to all, at the fore for their blessing. With song they honor you, the wide-famed, the one with listening ears, the divine one, through the human ages.

sanskrit: yasya tvaṃ sakhyamāvitha prabhañjansenāḥ pramṛṇo yudhā jayannasmākamedhyavitā rathānām
english: He whose friendship you have taken up — you who shatter armies, you who crush in battle and conquer — be the strengthener of our chariots.

sanskrit: tvāmicchavasaspate yanti giro na saṃyataḥ tava drapso nīlavānvāśa ṛtviya indhānaḥ siṣṇavā dade . tvaṃ mahīnāmuṣasāmasi priyaḥ kṣapo vastuṣu rājasi balavijñāyaḥ sthaviraḥ pravīraḥ sahasvānvājī sahamāna ugraḥ . abhivīro abhisatvā sahojā jaitramindra rathamā tiṣṭha govit
english: O lord of strength, to you the hymns proceed unhindered; your dark-gleaming drop, the seasonal one, blazing, eagerly takes hold. You are dear to the great dawns; you rule at the points of night; you are known by strength, steadfast, chief hero, powerful, victorious, fierce and overpowering. O Indra, hero above heroes, true champion, born of might — mount the winning chariot, winner of cattle.

sanskrit: vi srutayo yathā pathā indra tvadyantu rātayaḥ gotrabhidaṃ govidaṃ vajrabāhuṃ jayantamajma pramṛṇantamojasā . imaṃ sajātā anu vīrayadhvamindraṃ sakhāyo anu saṃ rabhadhvam
english: As streams flow by their paths, O Indra, may your gifts flow forth — him who splits the mountain-fortresses, who wins cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who conquers in the charge, who crushes the foe with force. O kinsmen, strive heroically after this Indra; O friends, rally together after him.

sanskrit: tuvikūrmimṛtīṣahamindraṃ śaviṣṭha satpatim tamitsamānaṃ vaninaśca vīrudho 'ntarvatīśca suvate ca viśvahā duścyavanaśca pṛtanāṣāḍayudhyo3 'smākaṃ senā avatu pra yutsu
english: The greatly active Indra, the crusher of enemies, the mightiest, the good lord — him do the forest trees and plants, the pregnant ones, and the bearing ones all forever bring forth. He who is hard to move and conquers armies with his weapons — may he protect our army, ever forward in battle.

sanskrit: tuviśuṣma tuvikrato śacīvo viśvayā mate . ā paprātha mahitvanā indra āsāṃ netā bṛhaspatirdakṣiṇā yajñaḥ pura etu somaḥ . devasenānāmabhibhañjatīnāṃ jayantīnāṃ maruto yantvagram
english: O greatly vigorous, greatly spirited, mighty one, with all wisdom you have filled all with your greatness, O Indra. May Brihaspati be the leader of these, the sacrifice the right hand, and Soma go before. May the Maruts march at the head of the divine armies, the overwhelming, victorious ones.

sanskrit: yasya te mahinā mahaḥ pari jmāyantamīyatuḥ . hastā vajraṃ hiraṇyayam indrasya vṛṣṇo varuṇasya rājña ādityānāṃ marutāṃ śardha ugram . mahāmanasāṃ bhuvanacyavānāṃ ghoṣo devānāṃ jayatāmudasthāt
english: Whose two great hands, by his greatness, travel around the earth holding the golden thunderbolt — the shout of Indra the mighty, of King Varuna, of the Adityas, of the fierce troop of Maruts, of the great-minded ones who shake the worlds, of the conquering gods, has risen up.

sanskrit: sūro na rurukvāñchatātmā mahiṣīva vi jāyate udvṛtrahanvājināṃ vājinānyudrathānāṃ jayatāṃ yantu ghoṣāḥ
english: Like the sun stretching himself, like a great cow giving birth — let the shouts of the Vritra-slaying prize-winners, of the prize horses and the winning chariots go forth.

sanskrit: abhi dvijanmā trī rocanāni viśvā rajāṃsi śuśucano asthāt . hotā yajiṣṭho apāṃ sadhasthe asmākamindraḥ samṛteṣu dhvajeṣvasmākaṃ yā iṣavastā jayantu . asmākaṃ vīrā uttare bhavantvasmāṃ u devā avatā haveṣu
english: The twice-born one blazing forth stood over the three bright realms and all the spaces. The most sacrificing hotar at the seat of the waters — may our Indra be present at our banners in battle; may those arrows of ours that are shot win. May our heroes be supreme; may the gods also protect us in our calls.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa hotā yo dvijanmā viśvā dadhe vāryāṇi śravasyā . marto yo asmai sutuko dadāśa asau yā senā marutaḥ pareṣāmabhyeti na ojasā spardhamānā . tāṃ gūhata tamasāpavratena yathaiteṣāmanyo anyaṃ na jānāt
english: This is that hotar, the twice-born, who has held all desirable things for glory. The mortal who has offered well-pressed soma to him — that army of our enemies, O Maruts, that comes against us without matching our strength — conceal it in darkness by your spell, so that among them one shall not know another.

sanskrit: ṛdhyāmā ta ohaiḥ yo jāgāra tamayaṃ soma āha tavāhamasmi sakhye nyokāḥ abhi prehi nirdaha hṛtsu śokairandhenāmitrāstamasā sacantām
english: May we prosper through your calls. He who is awake — to him this Soma speaks: I am at home in your friendship. Go forward, burn them out with the griefs in their hearts; may the foes be shrouded in the blindness of darkness.

sanskrit: adhā hyagne kratorbhadrasya dakṣasya sādhoḥ . rathīrṛtasya bṛhato babhūtha pretā jayatā nara indro vaḥ śarma yacchatu . ugrā vaḥ santu bāhavo 'nādhṛṣyā yathāsatha
english: For thus, O Agni, of auspicious will, of skilled power, you have become the charioteer of great cosmic order. Go forward, conquer, O men; may Indra grant you shelter. May your arms be fierce and irresistible as befits you.

sanskrit: ebhirno arkairbhavā no arvāṅksvā3rṇa jyotiḥ . agne viśvebhiḥ sumanā anīkaiḥ avasṛṣṭā parā pata śaravye brahmasaṃśite . gacchāmitrānpra padyasva māmīṣāṃ kaṃ ca nocchiṣaḥ
english: With these our hymns, turn toward us; be our heavenly light. O Agni, well-pleased with all your flames — O arrow let loose, fly forth, the sacred word has sharpened you. Go to the enemies, speed to them; let none of these escape.

sanskrit: ā dāśuṣe jātavedo vahā tvamadyā devāṃ uṣarbudhaḥ agnirjāgāra tamayaṃ soma āha tavāhamasmi sakhye nyokāḥ maiṣāṃ mocyaghahāraśca nendra vayāṃsyenānanusaṃyantu sarvān
english: O Jatavedas, bring today the gods for the worshipper; you who wake at dawn — Agni is awake; to him this Soma says: I am at home in your friendship. O Indra, let not the sin-bearer be freed from them; may not even birds follow those enemies in any direction.

sanskrit: juṣṭo hi dūto asi havyavāhano 'gne rathīradhvarāṇām . sajūraśvibhyāmuṣasā suvīryamasme dhehi śravo bṛhat amitrasenāṃ maghavannasmāñchatruyatīmabhi . ubhau tāmindra vṛtrahannagniśca dahataṃ prati
english: You are the beloved messenger, O Agni, bearer of oblations, charioteer of sacrifices. Together with the Ashvins and the Dawn, place great renown and heroic strength in us. O bountiful one, the enemy army that marches against us as our foe — both you, O Indra the Vritra-slayer, and Agni, burn it in return.

sanskrit: yatra bāṇāḥ sampatanti kumārā viśikhā iva . tatrā no brahmaṇaspatiraditiḥ śarma yacchatu viśvāhā śarma yacchatu
english: Where arrows fly together like young boys with bared tips — there may Brahmanaspati and Aditi grant us shelter; may they grant shelter forever.

sanskrit: devasya paśya kāvyaṃ mahitvādyā mamāra sa hyaḥ samāna yuñje vācaṃ śatapadīm vi manyumindra vṛtrahannamitrasyābhidāsataḥ
english: Behold the divine wisdom and greatness — one who was equal yesterday has died today. I yoke the hundred-footed speech. O Indra, O Vritra-slayer, turn your wrath against the enemy who assaults us.

sanskrit: śākmanā śāko aruṇaḥ suparṇa ā yo mahaḥ śūraḥ sanādanīḍaḥ . yacciketa satyamittanna moghaṃ vasu spārhamuta jetota dātā yuñje vācaṃ śatapadīṃ gāye sahasravarttani . gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jagat vi na indra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ . yo asmāṃ abhidāsatyadharaṃ gamayā tamaḥ
english: By his might the reddish fair-winged one is mighty, the great ancient hero without a nest. What he discerns is truly not in vain — desirable wealth, and he both wins and gives. I yoke the hundred-footed speech; I sing in the thousand-wheeled track. The Gayatri, the Trishtubh, the Jagati — O Indra, smite our enemies, press down those who attack us. Whoever assaults us, drive him down into darkness.

sanskrit: aibhirdade vṛṣṇyā pauṃsyāni yebhiraukṣadvṛtrahatyāya vajrī . ye karmaṇaḥ kriyamāṇasya mahna ṛtekarmamudajāyanta devāḥ gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jagadviśvā rūpāṇi sambhṛtā . devā okāṃsi cakrire indrasya bāhū sthavirau yuvānāvanādhṛṣyau supratīkāvasahyau . tau yuñjīta prathamau yoga āgate yābhyāṃ jitamasurāṇāṃ saho mahat
english: With these he took on the virile heroic powers with which the thunderbolt-wielder was anointed for the slaying of Vritra. The gods who were born by the greatness of the deed being done in cosmic order — the Gayatri, Trishtubh, Jagati, all forms gathered together — the gods made their dwelling. Indra's two arms, strong, youthful, irresistible, of fine aspect, unyielding — yoke those two first when the moment of union arrives, with which the great power of the Asuras was conquered.

sanskrit: uta svarājo aśvinā sūryo jyotirjyotiḥ sūryaḥ urorvarīyo varuṇaste kṛṇotu jayantaṃ tvānu devā madantu
english: And the self-ruling Ashvins, the Sun, light of lights is the Sun — may Varuna make for you the widest freedom; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.

sanskrit: pibanti mitro aryamā tanā pūtasya varuṇaḥ . triṣadhasthasya jāvataḥ punarūrjā ni varttasva punaragna iṣāyuṣā . punarnaḥ pāhyaṃhasaḥ andhā amitrā bhavatāśīrṣāṇo 'haya iva . teṣāṃ vo agninunnānāmindro hantu varaṃvaram
english: Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuna drink of the pure, the three-seated, the swift one. Return with strength; O Agni, return with food and life. Protect us again from sin. May the enemies be blind, headless like snakes — of those driven out by Agni, may Indra slay each one.

sanskrit: uto nvasya joṣamā indraḥ sutasya gomataḥ . prātarhoteva matsati saha rayyā ni vartasvāgne pinvasva dhārayā . viśvapsnyā viśvataspari yo naḥ svo 'raṇo yaśca niṣṭyo jighāṃsati . devāstaṃ sarve dhūrvantu brahma varma mamāntaraṃ śarma varma mamāntaram
english: And now may Indra take delight in this pressed soma with its cattle; like the morning hotar he shall rejoice together with wealth. Return, O Agni; swell with your stream. All-nourishing, encompassing all — whoever among our own kinsmen is estranged and whoever from outside seeks to slay us — may all the gods confound him. The sacred word is my inner armor and shelter, my inner armor.

sanskrit: mahaste sato mahimā paniṣtama mahnā deva mahāṃ asi stotā me gosakhā syāt sṛkaṃ saṃśāya pavimindra tigmaṃ vi śatrūṃ tāḍhi vi mṛdho nudasva
english: Great is your greatness, O most praiseworthy, great as you are; by your greatness, O god, you are great. May my praiser be a companion in cattle-wealth. O Indra, sharpen your bright sharp point; strike the enemies, thrust away the adversaries.
